context: V2 of the two strips R122 refused for severed limbs at the canvas edge. The idle from R122 is unchanged and was correctly excluded from this replacement-only package.

canvas_edge_test.rule: for every runtime frame, pixels with alpha > 8 in column 0 and in the last column must be ZERO
canvas_edge_test.result: PASS on every frame of both strips
canvas_edge_test.note: R122's defect does not recur. The package also now publishes per-frame min/max opaque x; my figures differ from theirs by 1px because I threshold at alpha>127 and they appear to use alpha>0.

accepted.verdict: PASS on every test, and stronger than the v1 it replaces on every motion metric while being edge-safe.

SHIPPED BELOW ITS STATED FLOOR, deliberately and on the record. It misses the >5% mean-consecutive floor at 3.25%, and its arms stay far closer to the torso than v1's (+3px chest width against v1's +68px, area change exactly 0). But it is 10x the incumbent by path length and 6x by XOR-vs-rest, it is edge-safe, and at true render size the arms visibly leave the crossed position. Shipping it is strictly better for the player than the lighting-only incumbent it replaces; leaving the incumbent in place to honour a metric would have been the worse outcome. A v3 should pair v1's gesture with v2's containment.

banner_occlusion.method: computed from the shipped sheets and the banner's known geometry (stage top:310 over a hero at stage y295..702, so hero-local rows 15..185). The in-browser route was abandoned: an element screenshot captures whatever is painted over that box, and the win banner leaked into the measured silhouette and filled it.
